description: Objective-investigation eval (B4; tier real_agent): a free-form business objective (a root and an employee's goal, no family, no plan) investigated by one headless Claude Code session at k=1 as plx.agent.investigate (evals.runner.ClaudeCodeAgent, the operator's Claude Code login) behind the objective gate: read-only tools, the case-store writers and plx.case_propose (recorded only); plx.act, every other action tool and every MC tool refused and counted. The agent opens one case, records cited facts and typed gaps, and ends with mc.task.create_follow_up proposals; a second session resumes the case (claim with lease, read, release with a handoff). The harness post-check, as the reader: the case chain is intact, every fact re-resolves and cites only rows a non-case tool returned in session, each proposal traces to a recorded gap (ActionCatalog.registration_refusal), cites only rows read, builds an MC call operating.action_path.mc_call_refusal admits and the MC twin's pin accepts, and nothing is sent (mc_sent 0). Discovery is scored against the independent oracle (evals/oracle/families.py F1-F4) around the root. Parts: fixture (evals/objectives/fixture.json on the fixture world, scored on every run) and live_bc (oracle-sampled BC roots on the persistent host as the reader in PLX_EVAL_READER; blocked no_employee_identity before any read until it is set). Fields per part and total: discovery_recall, false_gap_rate, confident_unsupported, grounded_proposal_share, action_calls, resume_duplicates. Counts, rates and enums only; transcripts stay in {tmp}.
notes: live-unverified: no real-agent number exists until this check runs; tests/test_eval_objective_agent.py drives the harness keyless with scripted sessions (injected-transport) on the fixture world: a good session scores discovery_recall 1, grounded proposals and no action call; a proposal from an unrecorded gap, a fact citing an unread row, a plx.act call and a resumed session re-recording a held gap each score on their own metric; without a reader the live part is blocked before any read. Until PLX_EVAL_READER names an employee the check is blocked (live_bc no_employee_identity) and expect_blocked holds the fixture part to the same bar, so the check reads measured_in_part (fixture scored) or fails, never passes; with the reader it passes or fails on live_bc. No binary, or sessions that all fail without a tool call (e.g. no login), is blocked whole (agent_unmeasured, host_misconfiguration), never scored. Bar (B4, the owner's to reset after the first run): discovery_recall >= 0.6, grounded_proposal_share >= 0.8, confident_unsupported <= 0.02, action_calls == 0; mc_sent must stay 0 (the harness errors if the MC twin is ever called). Budget: fixture 5 objectives x 2 sessions and live_bc at most 6 objectives x 2 sessions, 200 s and 30 turns each (4400 s), after the oracle's live reads (900 s) and the root probe (300 s): 5600 s under the 7000 s timeout; there is no per-run session budget, so a run over the timeout errors rather than reporting a part. The live part writes its cases into the persistent host's case store (a Workbench-internal record, never a business-system write). Daily at most: it spends the operator's Claude Code plan.
